title: cinna-agent.json
description: Definitional metadata for a locally built agent. Lives at the agent folder root and travels unchanged into a cloud agent workspace and into bundle revisions. Unknown keys are preserved for forward compatibility.
$comment: Every property carries two annotation keywords (contract 1.5.0; unknown keywords are legal JSON Schema 2020-12 annotations and change no validation outcome). `x-scope` is `portable` when every host gives the field the same meaning, `host` when it is interpreted only by the host that wrote it, or `host:<name>` when it is registered to one named host so nobody reuses the name - other hosts preserve such a field and ignore it. `x-import` says what `cinna agent import` does with the field: `imported`, `ignored`, or a short phrase naming the mapping. `ignored` means the import maps the value onto nothing; the key itself still travels, because the whole manifest is copied into the cloud workspace. A host may ship a field before it is registered here; every host preserves it and the import ignores it.

allOf.$comment: Identity is required of every folder scaffolded at contract 1.0.0 or later, and tolerated as absent in exactly one case: a legacy folder, which carries the integer schema_version and neither contract_version nor id. Such a folder must still parse - it is read, reported, and re-stamped - which is why contract_version and id are not in the top-level `required`. Any other manifest needs both. This encodes the same rule as the desktop's checkIdentity() and the CHANGELOG's Compatibility table; if you change one, change all three.

then.$comment: Legacy folder: read it, warn, ask for a re-stamp.

contract_version.description: Version of the folder contract this agent was scaffolded against, and the compatibility gate: a tool whose contract major is older than this must refuse to operate the folder. Required of every folder except a legacy one (see the top-level allOf).
contract_version.x-import: compatibility gate (a newer major is refused, an older or missing one warns); recorded in the publications.json entry

id.description: Stable identity of this agent, written once at scaffold and never rewritten. Survives folder moves and slug renames; preserved through cloud import as the agent's local origin. Required of every folder except a legacy one (see the top-level allOf).

schema_version.description: Legacy manifest version. A manifest that carries it, and neither contract_version nor id, is a pre-1.0.0 folder: it still parses, and a tool should re-stamp it rather than reject it. It is no longer the compatibility gate and nothing should branch on its value.
schema_version.x-import: legacy check: must be an integer, and a value above 1 is refused

kit_version.description: Version of the kit that scaffolded this agent. Informational only - never a gate.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp written by the scaffolder. Informational.

name.x-import: imported (the cloud agent's name; `--name` overrides it)

slug.description: Folder name and cloud reference. Must equal the agent folder's name.
slug.x-import: checked against the folder name; not sent

description.description: One sentence describing what the agent does. Feeds agent cards, the A2A card and router-trigger generation.

example_prompts.description: Ready-to-send task suggestions AND a first-class routing input. At least one is required for a cloud-ready agent.

router_trigger_prompt.description: One capability-verb sentence used only by the routing classifier. Describes when to route here, never how to behave.

prompts.description: Paths, relative to the agent root, of the three document-backed prompts.
prompts.x-import: each named file's contents become the cloud agent's prompt of that kind

runtime.description: How this agent should be run by a host that offers a choice. Absent means the host's default runtime. Never contains a secret: credential is a reference, not a key. Everything but `engine` stays local: the cloud runs an imported agent on the model and credential its own environment selects.
runtime.x-import: only `engine` is carried; see each property

engine.description: Which engine the author prefers to run the agent on - a preference, never a requirement. Known values: `opencode` (an OpenCode server), `claude` (Claude Code) and `codex` (the Codex CLI); `claude` and `codex` drive a CLI under its own login. Absent means the host's default engine. A host that does not support the named engine - including a value it does not recognise - runs the agent on OpenCode and never refuses the folder. Deliberately not an enum: a newer minor may name an engine this schema predates, and such a folder must still validate. `claude`/`codex` and `credential` are not meaningful together: those engines spend no host credential, so a host ignores the credential and a validator warns. Minted by Cinna Desktop as contract 1.2.0; part of the one contract since 1.5.0.
engine.x-import: engine preference -> the cloud environment's SDK at agent creation (`claude` -> claude-code, anything else -> opencode); an existing agent's engine is not changed

model.description: Model identifier as the host names it. Local only: the cloud import does not carry it, and an imported agent runs on the model its cloud environment selects. Mutually exclusive with `complexity`.

complexity.description: How hard this agent's work is, as a portable alternative to a concrete model id: the host resolves it against the models the chosen credential actually offers. Known tiers: `simple`, `medium`, `complex`. Deliberately not an enum, for the same reason as `engine`: a newer minor may add a tier, and an older strict validator must not reject that folder. A host that does not recognise the value runs the agent on its default model, and a validator warns. Mutually exclusive with `model`; a manifest carrying both is a warning and the model wins. Minted by Cinna Desktop as contract 1.1.0; part of the one contract since 1.5.0. Local only: there is no cloud counterpart yet.

credential.description: Reference to the AI credential to run on: a credential type, or the name of a credential configured in the host. NEVER a key, token or secret value. Local only: the cloud import does not carry it.

permissions.description: Host-specific permission profile for the agent's own tools. Interpreted by the host that wrote it; unknown keys are preserved.

status_refresh_command.description: Shell command, or a /run:<name> reference into docs/CLI_COMMANDS.yaml, executed before the platform reads STATUS.md.

credentials.description: Credential slots the agent needs. Never contains secret values.
credentials.x-import: each slot becomes an empty credential draft attached to the agent (reused by name when one exists)

name.x-import: imported (the draft's name, and the match key for an existing credential)

type.description: A platform credential type. The values below are the types known at contract 1.0.0; they are advisory, not a closed set. The platform's list grows independently of any bundled contract, so a contract pinned in a shipped desktop build cannot track it - an unrecognised value is therefore tolerated here and reported as a warning, and is resolved against the authoritative list at import.

service_uri.description: Explicit service slot for matching attached credentials of this type. Without it, match the declared name to the credential name or service_uri.

env_prefix.description: Prefix of the local .env variable names for this slot. Variable name is <env_prefix><FIELD in upper case>.

fields.description: Field names of the credential payload, as the platform names them.

schedules.description: Unattended run declarations. Platform import creates them as cloud schedules. Cinna Desktop may also run static_prompt schedules locally, only after a separate per-profile opt-in on each device and only while the app is open.
schedules.x-import: each entry becomes a cloud schedule, matched by name; an existing one is updated only with --update

description.description: What the schedule does, shown with the cloud schedule.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name. The cloud import uses it as the schedule's timezone, UTC when absent. A desktop opt-in freezes this zone, or the current system zone when absent, for matching local schedule occurrences.

prompt.description: Required for static_prompt: the message sent to start the run.

command.description: Required for script_trigger: the shell command whose non-OK output starts a session.

handovers.description: Other agents this one may delegate to. A target is the slug of a sibling agent, unless a host-registered `target_kind` gives the entry another meaning: Cinna Desktop reads the exact pair target_kind=coordinator, target_slug=coordinator as an explicit return to the coordinator that owns the current task.

target_kind.description: Optional host role, deliberately without an enum. Absent keeps sibling-slug semantics, including for a sibling literally named coordinator. The exact pair target_kind=coordinator and target_slug=coordinator enables Cinna Desktop's coordinator handback; target_kind=coordinator with any other slug is an error. Any other value grants no execution authority on the desktop. Minted by Cinna Desktop as contract 1.3.0; registered here since 1.5.0.

features.description: Cloud-only capabilities the agent expects once imported. Ignored locally.

cloud.description: DEPRECATED, replaced by the publications[] ledger, which lives in the sibling file publications.json and not in this one. Still accepted so a folder written before contract 1.0.0 parses; a tool that writes this manifest for any other reason migrates it into publications.json and drops the key. Never migrated at export time - an export must not mutate the manifest.
cloud.x-import: fallback: names the agent to update when publications.json has no entry for this instance

platform_url.x-import: the fallback applies only when absent or equal to this instance
